criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a claude.rs test feeds a fake driver reply with the text "You've hit your weekly limit · resets Oct 29, 6pm (UTC)" and no usage, and asserts the reply is recognised as a usage limit with the reset time parsed.
criteria.evidence: Three tests passed. a_weekly_limit_reply_is_a_usage_limit_with_its_reset_time passes the result line through StreamState::on_line and output_from_result. It asserts outcome Limited, a detail starting 'usage limit (resets at 2026-10-29T18:00:00Z): ' that contains the reply text, cost Some(0.0), zero usage that is not measured, and no models used. other_limit_kinds_and_reset_forms_are_understood covers session, 5-hour, daily and dated replies, and gives None for a non-UTC zone or no time. The stand-in test a_usage_limit_reply_from_the_child_is_a_limited_invocation_at_zero_cost goes through ClaudeCodeDriver::invoke with MODE=limit.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a run-level test with a fake driver returning the limit reply asserts the invocation record is marked limited with zero cost, passes the gate, the job stays retryable with its candidate kept, and no failure is counted.
criteria.evidence: a_usage_limit_at_the_verifier_holds_the_job_and_keeps_its_candidate_for_a_retry passed. Its verifier double reads the limit line through the real output_from_result. The test asserts: Failed with a reason starting 'environment: usage limit'; is_environment_reason is true; one Limited verifier record with cost 0 and no models; athena_gate::reconcile::check_invocation returns no violations; a candidate fingerprint and a Verifier resume mark exist. After restoring the plain driver, retry lands the same fingerprint, and the planner and producer counters stay at (0,1). The drain half of 'no failure counted' is shown under criterion 3.

It asserts Stop::UsageLimit with label 'usage limit' and usage_limit 'resets at 2026-10-29T18:00:00Z'. findings.summary: Drain still stops with 'repeated failure' when the usage limit is hit while it reads a request, the first model call it makes for each queued item.
findings.evidence: Found by reading the code; this scenario was not run. Drain notices a limit only through the run pipeline's closing reason (usage_limit_of in run_job). The reader call is not covered. For a queued item, drain's read step calls athena.go, which calls read_queued and runs the reader. reading.rs:483 turns any non-Success outcome, Limited included, into an ordinary reader error. drain.rs:798-809 turns that into RunStep::Failed, so failures is incremented, the item is read again, and after a second refusal drain stops as RepeatedFailure. Approval reads (drain.rs:1075) and retry reads go through the same reader. A weekly limit lasts days, so a drain started before the reset will most likely hit the limit at the reader first. That is the symptom the request asked to remove ('have drain stop with a usage limit stop reason ... instead of repeated failure'). Simpler, general alternative: have the reader report a Limited invocation as its own read outcome, or have drain check the job's records for a Limited invocation, and route it to RunStep::UsageLimit like the run step.

findings.summary: Three changed files are not on the expected deliverables list.
findings.evidence: git diff HEAD~1 --stat lists these files. They are not in the expected deliverables, but all three were in the accepted plan and are needed: the Limited enum variant, treating the usage-limit reason as an environment reason, and rendering the drain and status lines.

findings.summary: Drain recognises a limit by parsing the prefix of the job's closing-reason text, not from a structured field.
findings.evidence: run/mod.rs writes the reason 'environment: usage limit (resets at …)' and drain parses it back with usage_limit_of. This works and is tested, but it depends on the wording of a text string. A structured flag on the finished job would be sturdier.

summary: The change handles a usage limit correctly wherever a limit hit inside the run step is involved. The driver records a limit reply as Limited at zero cost, and the gate accepts it. A limited planner, critic, producer or verifier call closes the job as a failure of the environment, keeping the candidate for `athena retry`. Drain stops with 'usage limit' and the reset time without counting a failure, and `athena status` shows the limit until it resets. Ordinary errors are unchanged. All seven criteria are met: I ran the targeted tests and they passed, and Athena's fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. The verdict is still fail on one major finding. Drain only notices a limit through the run pipeline's closing reason, so a limit hit when drain reads a queued request (its first model call per item) is still counted as a failure and ends as 'repeated failure'. A weekly limit lasts days, so that is the likely case on the next drain before the reset. The fix is to route a Limited reader call to the same usage-limit stop.
